claims.claim: Mathematical structure is ontologically prior to physical reality. Math came first. Matter came second.
claims.plain_english: Math exists before and independently of the physical universe, and the universe is built from math, not the other way around.
claims.evidence_given: The 13.8 billion year gap: the universe obeyed mathematical laws before humans existed. The asymmetry table showing mathematical truth has opposite properties from human inventions. Wigner's unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics. The five limitation theorems showing closed systems cannot certify themselves.
claims.what_would_break_it: Producing a mathematical truth that is contingent, temporal, or local. Showing that math is a human invention that retroactively governed a pre-human universe.

claims.claim: The universe operated according to mathematical law for 13.8 billion years before any human mind existed to observe, formalize, or invent anything.
claims.plain_english: The universe followed math rules long before people were around to make up math.
claims.evidence_given: Cosmological timeline: universe age ~13.8 billion years, Homo sapiens ~300,000 years ago, written math ~5,000 years ago. Physical laws (inverse-square, Maxwell's equations, Schrödinger equation) operated before humans.
claims.what_would_break_it: Evidence that the universe did not obey consistent mathematical laws before humans. Showing that physical laws are retroactive human projections with no prior reality.

claims.claim: Nominalism (math is invented) fails because it cannot explain how a human invention governed a universe that predated its inventors by 13.8 billion years.
claims.plain_english: If math is just something people made up, it shouldn't work for the universe before people existed.
claims.evidence_given: The temporal gap argument. The claim that nominalists either concede the patterns were always there (making math a discovery, not invention) or must accept that all physics is fictional.
claims.what_would_break_it: Showing that mathematical patterns are not intrinsic to the universe but are imposed by human minds. Demonstrating that pre-human physical processes did not actually follow mathematical regularities.

claims.claim: Platonism (math is abstract) fails because abstract objects have no causal power, yet mathematical laws enforce compliance on physical systems like bridges and orbits.
claims.plain_english: If math exists in a separate non-physical world, it can't make bridges stay up or planets follow orbits.
claims.evidence_given: The causal problem: abstract objects cannot push, pull, or constrain. Bridges that violate equations collapse. Orbits that deviate from Kepler's laws self-correct. Platonism offers no mechanism for this enforcement.
claims.what_would_break_it: Explaining how causally inert abstract objects can constrain physical systems. Showing that mathematical laws are merely descriptive, not prescriptive.

claims.claim: Fictionalism (math is useful fiction) fails because a false theory cannot reliably generate true predictions to fourteen decimal places.
claims.plain_english: If math were made-up and false, it wouldn't work so perfectly to predict real things.
claims.evidence_given: Analogy: a fictional map of London won't get you to Paddington Station. A fictional theory of chemistry won't produce working drugs. Math is the only 'fiction' that predicts reality with extreme precision.
claims.what_would_break_it: Showing that mathematical predictions are not uniquely reliable. Demonstrating that fictional models in other domains can produce accurate predictions.

claims.claim: Wigner's 'unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics' is resolved if math is ontologically prior to physics: physical reality is an instantiation of mathematical structure.
claims.plain_english: The mystery of why math works so well goes away if the universe is actually made of math.
claims.evidence_given: Examples: non-Euclidean geometry developed as pure math later used for relativity. Complex numbers as algebraic abstractions required by quantum mechanics. Group theory as pure math used in particle physics.
claims.what_would_break_it: Producing an alternative explanation for Wigner's effectiveness that does not presuppose ontological priority. Showing that mathematical concepts developed for abstract reasons do not match physical reality.

claims.claim: Five independent limitation theorems (Gödel, Tarski, Turing, Second Law, Landauer) converge on the conclusion that closed systems cannot certify themselves, implying mathematical structure governing physical reality must come from outside physical reality.
claims.plain_english: Several different math and science proofs all say the same thing: a system can't prove itself true, so the math that runs the universe must come from outside the universe.
claims.evidence_given: Gödel's incompleteness (1931), Tarski's undefinability (1933), Turing's halting problem (1936), Second Law of Thermodynamics (1850s), Landauer's principle (1961). All show that no system can fully certify or ground itself from within.
claims.what_would_break_it: Showing that the five theorems do not actually converge on the same structural conclusion. Demonstrating that a closed system can certify itself. Providing a physical grounding for mathematical truth.

claims.claim: Mathematical truth and human invention are categorically mismatched across seven properties: existence, duration, stability, scope, substrate, role, and reliability.
claims.plain_english: Math and human-made things are completely different in every important way.
claims.evidence_given: Asymmetry table: mathematical truth is necessary, eternal, immutable, universal, immaterial, foundational, infallible. Human invention is contingent, temporal, mutable, local, material, derivative, fallible.
claims.what_would_break_it: Showing that the property comparison uses flawed categories. Demonstrating that mathematical truth is contingent, temporal, mutable, or local in any meaningful sense.

claims.claim: The paper can be falsified by producing a contingent, temporal, or local mathematical truth, or by explaining the causal efficacy of abstract objects without invoking agency.
claims.plain_english: This argument can be proven wrong if you can show math changes depending on time, place, or situation, or if you can explain how non-physical math affects physical things.
claims.evidence_given: Five specific falsification criteria are listed: contingent truth, temporal truth, local truth, causal abstract objects, alternative to Wigner. None have been accomplished.
claims.what_would_break_it: Successfully producing any of the five falsification criteria. Showing that the criteria are impossible in principle or irrelevant.

claims.claim: The argument stands or falls on logic, not on the author's theological beliefs, and can be defeated structurally by attacking the method, the data, or producing a better compression.
claims.plain_english: You don't need to know what the author believes about God to judge whether this argument is correct. You just need to check the logic and evidence.
claims.evidence_given: The Biaxiosum rule: name your ground before critiquing. Three moves for engagement: attack method, attack data, produce better compression. Credential objections and appeals to consensus are excluded.
claims.what_would_break_it: Showing that the argument secretly depends on theological assumptions. Demonstrating that the three moves are impossible or irrelevant. Showing that credential or consensus objections are structurally valid.
